question: Intramuscular injections and aspirin should be avoided in children with haemophilia because IM injections risk expanding haematomas and aspirin inhibits platelet function, worsening bleeding.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Both IM injections and aspirin are absolutely contraindicated in haemophilia. IM injections cause haematomas; aspirin impairs platelet function. Use SC injections and paracetamol instead.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. IM injections can cause expanding, expanding intramuscular haematomas that compress neurovascular structures in a child with haemophilia. Aspirin irreversibly inhibits COX-1/thromboxane A2 platelet aggregation, further impairing primary haemostasis. Always use subcutaneous routes and paracetamol for analgesia.
